summary:
We developed FireCalendar, a web application that turns 25 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots (2000–2025) into a consistent burning activity calendar for any area: a country, one of over 4,000 provinces, a drawn polygon or an uploaded boundary.
It addresses the challenge by harmonizing the MODIS and VIIRS records, which cannot be compared directly because VIIRS detects several times more hotspots. A machine-learning model converts MODIS counts to the NOAA-20 VIIRS scale, with about 15% median error on years it never saw. On this single record, users can see which months and years burned most, compare the current month with its historical median, spot unusual fire seasons, rank provinces and download automatically written reports.
This matters because MODIS is nearing retirement. Without harmonization, the switch between sensors looks like a surge in fire and hides real change. FireCalendar keeps the 25-year record usable, giving emergency responders, scientists and land managers early warning of critical periods.
details:
FireCalendar is a web application that turns 25 years of NASA FIRMS active-fire detections (2000–2025) into one consistent burning activity calendar for any area on Earth: a country, one of over 4,000 provinces and states, a drawn polygon or an uploaded boundary.

MODIS and VIIRS records cannot be compared directly. VIIRS's finer pixels record about seven times as many hotspots as Aqua MODIS, so the switch between sensors looks like a surge in fire. We harmonize about 270 million detections to the NOAA-20 VIIRS scale with a machine-learning conversion model built on both MODIS satellites, Terra and Aqua. Tested on years it never saw, it has a median error of about 15% for 1° cells and under 10% for large regions. Its 90% uncertainty range is carried into the results, and static heat sources such as gas flares and volcanoes are removed.

On this consistent record, users can see which months and years burned most and compare the current month with its historical median. They can spot unusual periods (the app flags Australia's Black Summer and Canada's record 2023 season), rank provinces, and read automatically written reports with downloadable data.

As MODIS nears retirement, FireCalendar keeps its 25-year record usable alongside VIIRS. It gives emergency responders, scientists and land managers early warning of critical periods and abnormal fire seasons.
